heading: Food additives
body_text: (C) the number of study protocols that have been pending review for over 50 days, and the number that have received an extension.
top_caption: Food additives intended for use in animal food
label: FD&C Act § 409(k)(2)(C) [21 U.S.C. 348(k)(2)(C)]

heading: Food additives
body_text: (3) In the case of a food additive petition intended for use in animal food, the Secretary shall provide information to the petitioner on the required contents of such petition. If the Secretary requires additional studies beyond what the petitioner proposed, the Secretary shall provide the scientific rationale for such requirement.
top_caption: Food additives intended for use in animal food
label: FD&C Act § 409(k)(3) [21 U.S.C. 348(k)(3)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: An infant formula, including an infant formula powder, shall be deemed to be adulterated if—
label: FD&C Act § 412(a) [21 U.S.C. 350a(a)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) such infant formula does not provide nutrients as required by subsection (i),
label: FD&C Act § 412(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(a)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) such infant formula does not meet the quality factor requirements prescribed by the Secretary under subsection (b)(1), or
label: FD&C Act § 412(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(a)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (3) the processing of such infant formula is not in compliance with the good manufacturing practices and the quality control procedures prescribed by the Secretary under subsection (b)(2).
label: FD&C Act § 412(a)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350a(a)(3)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) The Secretary shall by regulation establish requirements for quality factors for infant formulas to the extent possible consistent with current scientific knowledge, including quality factor requirements for the nutrients required by subsection (i).
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2)(A) The Secretary shall by regulation establish good manufacturing practices for infant formulas, including quality control procedures that the Secretary determines are necessary to assure that an infant formula provides nutrients in accordance with this subsection and subsection (i) and is manufactured in a manner designed to prevent adulteration of the infant formula.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) The good manufacturing practices and quality control procedures prescribed by the Secretary under subparagraph (A) shall include requirements for—
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (i) the testing, in accordance with paragraph (3) and by the manufacturer of an infant formula or an agent of such manufacturer, of each batch of infant formula for each nutrient required by subsection (i) before the distribution of such batch,
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)(i)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (ii) regularly scheduled testing, by the manufacturer of an infant formula or an agent of such manufacturer, of samples of infant formulas during the shelf life of such formulas to ensure that such formulas are in compliance with this section,
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)(ii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (iii) in-process controls including, where necessary, testing required by good manufacturing practices designed to prevent adulteration of each batch of infant formula, and
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B)(iii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)(iii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (iv) the conduct by the manufacturer of an infant formula or an agent of such manufacturer of regularly scheduled audits to determine that such manufacturer has complied with the regulations prescribed under subparagraph (A).
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B)(iv) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)(iv)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: In prescribing requirements for audits under clause (iv), the Secretary shall provide that such audits be conducted by appropriately trained individuals who do not have any direct responsibility for the manufacture or production of infant formula.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(2)(B)(iv) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(2)(B)(iv)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (3)(A) At the final product stage, each batch of infant formula shall be tested for vitamin A, vitamin B1, vitamin C, and vitamin E to ensure that such infant formula is in compliance with the requirements of this subsection and subsection (i) relating to such vitamins.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) Each nutrient premix used in the manufacture of an infant formula shall be tested for each relied upon nutrient required by subsection (i) which is contained in such premix to ensure that such premix is in compliance with its specifications or certifications by a premix supplier.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (C) During the manufacturing process or at the final product stage and before distribution of an infant formula, an infant formula shall be tested for all nutrients required to be included in such formula by subsection (i) for which testing has not been conducted pursuant to subparagraph (A) or (B). Testing under this subparagraph shall be conducted to—
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(C)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (i) ensure that each batch of such infant formula is in compliance with the requirements of subsection (i) relating to such nutrients, and
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(C)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(C)(i)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (ii) confirm that nutrients contained in any nutrient premix used in such infant formula are present in each batch of such infant formula in the proper concentration.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(C)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(C)(ii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (D) If the Secretary adds a nutrient to the list of nutrients in the table in subsection (i), the Secretary shall by regulation require that the manufacturer of an infant formula test each batch of such formula for such new nutrient in accordance with subparagraph (A), (B), or (C).
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(D)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (E) For purposes of this paragraph, the term "final product stage" means the point in the manufacturing process, before distribution of an infant formula, at which an infant formula is homogenous and is not subject to further degradation.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(3)(E) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(3)(E)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (4)(A) The Secretary shall by regulation establish requirements respecting the retention of records. Such requirements shall provide for—
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (i) the retention of all records necessary to demonstrate compliance with the good manufacturing practices and quality control procedures prescribed by the Secretary under paragraph (2), including records containing the results of all testing required under paragraph (2)(B),
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(i)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (ii) the retention of all certifications or guarantees of analysis by premix suppliers,
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(ii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (iii) the retention by a premix supplier of all records necessary to confirm the accuracy of all premix certifications and guarantees of analysis,
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(iii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(iii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (iv) the retention of—
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(iv) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(iv)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (I) all records pertaining to the microbiological quality and purity of raw materials used in infant formula powder and in finished infant formula, and
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(iv)(I) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(iv)(I)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (II) all records pertaining to food packaging materials which show that such materials do not cause an infant formula to be adulterated within the meaning of section 342(a)(2)(C) of this title,
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(iv)(II) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(iv)(II)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (v) the retention of all records of the results of regularly scheduled audits conducted pursuant to the requirements prescribed by the Secretary under paragraph (2)(B)(iv), and
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(v) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(v)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (vi) the retention of all complaints and the maintenance of files with respect to, and the review of, complaints concerning infant formulas which may reveal the possible existence of a hazard to health.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(A)(vi) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(A)(vi)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B)(i) Records required under subparagraph (A) with respect to an infant formula shall be retained for at least one year after the expiration of the shelf life of such infant formula. Except as provided in clause (ii), such records shall be made available to the Secretary for review and duplication upon request of the Secretary.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(B)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(B)(i)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (ii) A manufacturer need only provide written assurances to the Secretary that the regularly scheduled audits required by paragraph (2)(B)(iv) are being conducted by the manufacturer, and need not make available to the Secretary the actual written reports of such audits.
top_caption: Requirements for quality factors, good manufacturing practices, and retention of records
label: FD&C Act § 412(b)(4)(B)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350a(b)(4)(B)(ii)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) No person shall introduce or deliver for introduction into interstate commerce any new infant formula unless—
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) such person has, before introducing such new infant formula, or delivering such new infant formula for introduction, into interstate commerce, registered with the Secretary the name of such person, the place of business of such person, and all establishments at which such person intends to manufacture such new infant formula, and
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) such person has at least 90 days before marketing such new infant formula, made the submission to the Secretary required by subsection (d)(1).
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) For purposes of paragraph (1), the term "new infant formula" includes—
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) an infant formula manufactured by a person which has not previously manufactured an infant formula, and
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(2)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) an infant formula manufactured by a person which has previously manufactured infant formula and in which there is a major change, in processing or formulation, from a current or any previous formulation produced by such manufacturer.
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(2)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: For purposes of this paragraph, the term "major change" has the meaning given to such term in section 106.30(c)(2) of title 21, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on August 1, 1986), and guidelines issued thereunder.
top_caption: Registration of persons distributing new infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(c)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(c)(2)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) A person shall, with respect to any infant formula subject to subsection (c), make a submission to the Secretary which shall include—
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) the quantitative formulation of the infant formula,
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) a description of any reformulation of the formula or change in processing of the infant formula,
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (C) assurances that the infant formula will not be marketed unless it meets the requirements of subsections (b)(1) and (i), as demonstrated by the testing required under subsection (b)(3), and
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(1)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(1)(C)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (D) assurances that the processing of the infant formula complies with subsection (b)(2).
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(1)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(1)(D)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) After the first production of an infant formula subject to subsection (c), and before the introduction into interstate commerce of such formula, the manufacturer of such formula shall submit to the Secretary, in such form as may be prescribed by the Secretary, a written verification which summarizes test results and records demonstrating that such formula complies with the requirements of subsections (b)(1), (b)(2)(A), (b)(2)(B)(i), (b)(2)(B)(iii), (b)(3)(A), (b)(3)(C), and (i).
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (3) If the manufacturer of an infant formula for commercial or charitable distribution for human consumption determines that a change in the formulation of the formula or a change in the processing of the formula may affect whether the formula is adulterated under subsection (a), the manufacturer shall, before the first processing of such formula, make the submission to the Secretary required by paragraph (1).
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(3)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (4) The Secretary shall provide a response to a submission under this subsection not later than 45 days after receiving such submission.
top_caption: Submission of information about new infant formula required
label: FD&C Act § 412(d)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350a(d)(4)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) If the manufacturer of an infant formula has knowledge which reasonably supports the conclusion that an infant formula which has been processed by the manufacturer and which has left an establishment subject to the control of the manufacturer—
label: FD&C Act § 412(e)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(e)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) may not provide the nutrients required by subsection (i), or
label: FD&C Act § 412(e)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(e)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) may be otherwise adulterated or misbranded,
label: FD&C Act § 412(e)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(e)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: the manufacturer shall promptly notify the Secretary of such knowledge. If the Secretary determines that the infant formula presents a risk to human health, the manufacturer shall immediately take all actions necessary to recall shipments of such infant formula from all wholesale and retail establishments, consistent with recall regulations and guidelines issued by the Secretary.
label: FD&C Act § 412(e)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(e)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) For purposes of paragraph (1), the term "knowledge" as applied to a manufacturer means (A) the actual knowledge that the manufacturer had, or (B) the knowledge which a reasonable person would have had under like circumstances or which would have been obtained upon the exercise of due care.
label: FD&C Act § 412(e)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(e)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (f) Procedures applicable to recalls by manufacturer; regulatory oversight
label: FD&C Act § 412(f) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) If a recall of infant formula is begun by a manufacturer, the recall shall be carried out in accordance with such requirements as the Secretary shall prescribe under paragraph (2) and—
label: FD&C Act § 412(f)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) the Secretary shall, not later than the 15th day after the beginning of such recall and at least once every 15 days thereafter until the recall is terminated, review the actions taken under the recall to determine whether the recall meets the requirements prescribed under paragraph (2), and
label: FD&C Act § 412(f)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) the manufacturer shall, not later than the 14th day after the beginning of such recall and at least once every 14 days thereafter until the recall is terminated, report to the Secretary the actions taken to implement the recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(f)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) The Secretary shall by regulation prescribe the scope and extent of recalls of infant formulas necessary and appropriate for the degree of risks to human health presented by the formula subject to the recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(f)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (3) The Secretary shall by regulation require each manufacturer of an infant formula who begins a recall of such formula because of a risk to human health to request each retail establishment at which such formula is sold or available for sale to post at the point of purchase of such formula a notice of such recall at such establishment for such time that the Secretary determines necessary to inform the public of such recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(f)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350a(f)(3)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (g) Recordkeeping requirements for manufacturer; regulatory oversight and enforcement
label: FD&C Act § 412(g) [21 U.S.C. 350a(g)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) Each manufacturer of an infant formula shall make and retain such records respecting the distribution of the infant formula through any establishment owned or operated by such manufacturer as may be necessary to effect and monitor recalls of the formula. Such records shall be retained for at least one year after the expiration of the shelf life of the infant formula.
label: FD&C Act § 412(g)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(g)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) To the extent that the Secretary determines that records are not being made or maintained in accordance with paragraph (1), the Secretary may by regulation prescribe the records required to be made under paragraph (1) and requirements respecting the retention of such records under such paragraph. Such regulations shall take effect on such date as the Secretary prescribes but not sooner than the 180th day after the date such regulations are promulgated. Such regulations shall apply only with respect to distributions of infant formulas made after such effective date.
label: FD&C Act § 412(g)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(g)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (h) Exemptions; regulatory oversight
label: FD&C Act § 412(h) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) Any infant formula which is represented and labeled for use by an infant—
label: FD&C Act § 412(h)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) who has an inborn error of metabolism or a low birth weight, or
label: FD&C Act § 412(h)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) who otherwise has an unusual medical or dietary problem,
label: FD&C Act § 412(h)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: is exempt from the requirements of subsections (a), (b), and (c). The manufacturer of an infant formula exempt under this paragraph shall, in the case of the exempt formula, be required to provide the notice required by subsection (e)(1) only with respect to adulteration or misbranding described in subsection (e)(1)(B) and to comply with the regulations prescribed by the Secretary under paragraph (2).
label: FD&C Act § 412(h)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) The Secretary may by regulation establish terms and conditions for the exemption of an infant formula from the requirements of subsections (a), (b), and (c). An exemption of an infant formula under paragraph (1) may be withdrawn by the Secretary if such formula is not in compliance with applicable terms and conditions prescribed under this paragraph.
label: FD&C Act § 412(h)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (1) An infant formula shall contain nutrients in accordance with the table set out in this subsection, which shall be reviewed by the Secretary every 4 years as appropriate. In reviewing such table, the Secretary shall consider any new scientific data or information related to infant formula nutrients, including international infant formula standards. The Secretary may revise the list of nutrients and the required level for any nutrient required by the table.
label: FD&C Act § 412(i)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(i)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (2) The Secretary may by regulation—
label: FD&C Act § 412(i)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(i)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) revise the list of nutrients in the table in this subsection, and
label: FD&C Act § 412(i)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(i)(2)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) revise the required level for any nutrient required by the table.

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: The Secretary shall waive the 90-day premarket submission requirement under subsection (c) and apply a 30-day premarket submission requirement for any person who intends to introduce or deliver for introduction into interstate commerce any new infant formula.
label: FD&C Act § 412(j)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(j)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: The waiver authority under this subsection shall remain in effect—
label: FD&C Act § 412(j)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(j)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) for 90 days beginning on the date that the Secretary distributes information under section 350m(a)(2) of this title with respect to a shortage of infant formula; or
label: FD&C Act § 412(j)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(j)(2)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) such longer period as the Secretary determines appropriate, to prevent or mitigate a shortage of infant formula.
label: FD&C Act § 412(j)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(j)(2)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: Not later than 24 hours after the initiation of a recall of infant formula as described in subsection (e), the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a notification of such recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: A notification under paragraph (1) shall include the following:
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) If the recall is required by the Food and Drug Administration, a summary of the information supporting a determination that the adulterated or misbranded infant formula presents a risk to human health.
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(2)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) If the recall is voluntarily initiated by the manufacturer, a summary of the information provided to the Food and Drug Administration by the manufacturer regarding infant formula that has left the control of the manufacturer that may be adulterated or misbranded.
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(2)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (C) Specification of when the Food and Drug Administration was first made aware of the instance or circumstances surrounding the recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(2)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(2)(C)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (D) An initial estimate of the disruption in domestic production that may result from the recall.
label: FD&C Act § 412(k)(2)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350a(k)(2)(D)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: Not later than March 30 of each year, the Secretary shall submit a report to Congress containing, with respect to the preceding calendar year, the following information:
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) The number of submissions received by the Secretary under subsection (d).
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) The number of such submissions that included any new ingredients that were not included in any infant formula already on the market.
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (C) The number of inspections conducted by the Food and Drug Administration or any agent thereof to evaluate compliance with the requirements for infant formulas under subsection (b).
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)(C)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (D) The time between any inspection referred to in subparagraph (C) and any necessary reinspection to evaluate compliance with the requirements for infant formulas under subsection (b).
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)(D)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (E) A breakdown of the information described in subparagraphs (A) through (D) between foreign and domestic manufacturers and facilities.
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(1)(E) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(1)(E)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: The Secretary shall ensure that the reports under paragraph (1) do not include any information that is a trade secret or confidential information subject to section 552(b)(4) of title 5 or section 1905 of title 18.
label: FD&C Act § 412(l)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(l)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: The Secretary may, during a shortage of specialty infant formula as determined by the Secretary, waive any requirement under this chapter applicable to facilitate the importation of specialty infant formula. Such a waiver may be applicable to—
top_caption: Waiver of requirements for importation of specialty infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(m)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350a(m)(1)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (A) the importation of specialty infant formula from any country that is determined by the Secretary to be implementing and enforcing requirements for infant formula that provide a similar assurance of safety and nutritional adequacy as the requirements of this chapter; or
top_caption: Waiver of requirements for importation of specialty infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(m)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350a(m)(1)(A)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: (B) the distribution and sale of such imported specialty infant formula.
top_caption: Waiver of requirements for importation of specialty infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(m)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350a(m)(1)(B)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: Nothing in paragraph (1) shall be construed to limit the authority of the Secretary to require a recall of, or otherwise impose restrictions and requirements under this chapter with respect to, specialty infant formula that is subject to a waiver under paragraph (1).
top_caption: Waiver of requirements for importation of specialty infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(m)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350a(m)(2)]

heading: Infant formulas
body_text: In this subsection, the term "specialty infant formula" means infant formula described in subsection (h)(1).
top_caption: Waiver of requirements for importation of specialty infant formula
label: FD&C Act § 412(m)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350a(m)(3)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: A dietary supplement which contains a new dietary ingredient shall be deemed adulterated under section 342(f) of this title unless it meets one of the following requirements:
label: FD&C Act § 413(a) [21 U.S.C. 350b(a)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: (1) The dietary supplement contains only dietary ingredients which have been present in the food supply as an article used for food in a form in which the food has not been chemically altered.
label: FD&C Act § 413(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350b(a)(1)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: (2) There is a history of use or other evidence of safety establishing that the dietary ingredient when used under the conditions recommended or suggested in the labeling of the dietary supplement will reasonably be expected to be safe and, at least 75 days before being introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce, the manufacturer or distributor of the dietary ingredient or dietary supplement provides the Secretary with information, including any citation to published articles, which is the basis on which the manufacturer or distributor has concluded that a dietary supplement containing such dietary ingredient will reasonably be expected to be safe.
label: FD&C Act § 413(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350b(a)(2)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: The Secretary shall keep confidential any information provided under paragraph (2) for 90 days following its receipt. After the expiration of such 90 days, the Secretary shall place such information on public display, except matters in the information which are trade secrets or otherwise confidential, commercial information.
label: FD&C Act § 413(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350b(a)(2)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: Any person may file with the Secretary a petition proposing the issuance of an order prescribing the conditions under which a new dietary ingredient under its intended conditions of use will reasonably be expected to be safe. The Secretary shall make a decision on such petition within 180 days of the date the petition is filed with the Secretary. For purposes of chapter 7 of title 5, the decision of the Secretary shall be considered final agency action.
label: FD&C Act § 413(b) [21 U.S.C. 350b(b)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: If the Secretary determines that the information in a new dietary ingredient notification submitted under this section for an article purported to be a new dietary ingredient is inadequate to establish that a dietary supplement containing such article will reasonably be expected to be safe because the article may be, or may contain, an anabolic steroid or an analogue of an anabolic steroid, the Secretary shall notify the Drug Enforcement Administration of such determination. Such notification by the Secretary shall include, at a minimum, the name of the dietary supplement or article, the name of the person or persons who marketed the product or made the submission of information regarding the article to the Secretary under this section, and any contact information for such person or persons that the Secretary has.
label: FD&C Act § 413(c)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350b(c)(1)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: For purposes of this subsection—
label: FD&C Act § 413(c)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350b(c)(2)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: (A) the term "anabolic steroid" has the meaning given such term in section 802(41) of this title; and
label: FD&C Act § 413(c)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350b(c)(2)(A)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: (B) the term "analogue of an anabolic steroid" means a substance whose chemical structure is substantially similar to the chemical structure of an anabolic steroid.
label: FD&C Act § 413(c)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350b(c)(2)(B)]

heading: New dietary ingredients
body_text: For purposes of this section, the term "new dietary ingredient" means a dietary ingredient that was not marketed in the United States before October 15, 1994 and does not include any dietary ingredient which was marketed in the United States before October 15, 1994.
label: FD&C Act § 413(d) [21 U.S.C. 350b(d)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: If the Secretary has a reasonable belief that an article of food, and any other article of food that the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner, is adulterated and presents a threat of serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals, each person (excluding farms and restaurants) who manufactures, processes, packs, distributes, receives, holds, or imports such article shall, at the request of an officer or employee duly designated by the Secretary, permit such officer or employee, upon presentation of appropriate credentials and a written notice to such person, at reasonable times and within reasonable limits and in a reasonable manner, to have access to and copy all records relating to such article, and to any other article of food that the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner, that are needed to assist the Secretary in determining whether the food is adulterated and presents a threat of serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals.
label: FD&C Act § 414(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350c(a)(1)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
paragraph_heading: Use of or exposure to food of concern
body_text: If the Secretary believes that there is a reasonable probability that the use of or exposure to an article of food, and any other article of food that the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner, will cause serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals, each person (excluding farms and restaurants) who manufactures, processes, packs, distributes, receives, holds, or imports such article shall, at the request of an officer or employee duly designated by the Secretary, permit such officer or employee, upon presentation of appropriate credentials and a written notice to such person, at reasonable times and within reasonable limits and in a reasonable manner, to have access to and copy all records relating to such article and to any other article of food that the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner, that are needed to assist the Secretary in determining whether there is a reasonable probability that the use of or exposure to the food will cause serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals.
label: FD&C Act § 414(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350c(a)(2)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: The requirement under paragraphs (1) and (2) applies to all records relating to the manufacture, processing, packing, distribution, receipt, holding, or importation of such article maintained by or on behalf of such person in any format (including paper and electronic formats) and at any location.
label: FD&C Act § 414(a)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350c(a)(3)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: The Secretary, in consultation and coordination, as appropriate, with other Federal departments and agencies with responsibilities for regulating food safety, may by regulation establish requirements regarding the establishment and maintenance, for not longer than two years, of records by persons (excluding farms and restaurants) who manufacture, process, pack, transport, distribute, receive, hold, or import food, which records are needed by the Secretary for inspection to allow the Secretary to identify the immediate previous sources and the immediate subsequent recipients of food, including its packaging, in order to address credible threats of serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals. The Secretary shall take into account the size of a business in promulgating regulations under this section.
label: FD&C Act § 414(b) [21 U.S.C. 350c(b)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: The Secretary shall take appropriate measures to ensure that there are in effect effective procedures to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of any trade secret or confidential information that is obtained by the Secretary pursuant to this section.
label: FD&C Act § 414(c) [21 U.S.C. 350c(c)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: This section shall not be construed—
label: FD&C Act § 414(d) [21 U.S.C. 350c(d)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: (1) to limit the authority of the Secretary to inspect records or to require establishment and maintenance of records under any other provision of this chapter;
label: FD&C Act § 414(d)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350c(d)(1)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: (2) to authorize the Secretary to impose any requirements with respect to a food to the extent that it is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Secretary of Agriculture pursuant to the Federal Meat Inspection Act (21 U.S.C. 601 et seq.), the Poultry Products Inspection Act (21 U.S.C. 451 et seq.), or the Egg Products Inspection Act (21 U.S.C. 1031 et seq.);
label: FD&C Act § 414(d)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350c(d)(2)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: (3) to have any legal effect on section 552 of title 5 or section 1905 of title 18; or
label: FD&C Act § 414(d)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350c(d)(3)]

heading: Maintenance and inspection of records
body_text: (4) to extend to recipes for food, financial data, pricing data, personnel data, research data, or sales data (other than shipment data regarding sales).
label: FD&C Act § 414(d)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350c(d)(4)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The Secretary shall by regulation require that any facility engaged in manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding food for consumption in the United States be registered with the Secretary. To be registered—
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(1)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (A) for a domestic facility, the owner, operator, or agent in charge of the facility shall submit a registration to the Secretary; and
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(1)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (B) for a foreign facility, the owner, operator, or agent in charge of the facility shall submit a registration to the Secretary and shall include with the registration the name of the United States agent for the facility.
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(1)(B)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: An entity (referred to in this section as the "registrant") shall submit a registration under paragraph (1) to the Secretary containing information necessary to notify the Secretary of the name and address of each facility at which, and all trade names under which, the registrant conducts business, the e-mail address for the contact person of the facility or, in the case of a foreign facility, the United States agent for the facility, and, when determined necessary by the Secretary through guidance, the general food category (as identified under section 170.3 of title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, or any other food categories as determined appropriate by the Secretary, including by guidance) of any food manufactured, processed, packed, or held at such facility. The registration shall contain an assurance that the Secretary will be permitted to inspect such facility at the times and in the manner permitted by this chapter. The registrant shall notify the Secretary in a timely manner of changes to such information.
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(2)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: During the period beginning on October 1 and ending on December 31 of each even-numbered year, a registrant that has submitted a registration under paragraph (1) shall submit to the Secretary a renewal registration containing the information described in paragraph (2). The Secretary shall provide for an abbreviated registration renewal process for any registrant that has not had any changes to such information since the registrant submitted the preceding registration or registration renewal for the facility involved.
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(3)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: Upon receipt of a completed registration described in paragraph (1), the Secretary shall notify the registrant of the receipt of such registration and assign a registration number to each registered facility.
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(4)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The Secretary shall compile and maintain an up-to-date list of facilities that are registered under this section. Such list and any registration documents submitted pursuant to this subsection shall not be subject to disclosure under section 552 of title 5. Information derived from such list or registration documents shall not be subject to disclosure under section 552 of title 5 to the extent that it discloses the identity or location of a specific registered person.
label: FD&C Act § 415(a)(5) [21 U.S.C. 350d(a)(5)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: If the Secretary determines that food manufactured, processed, packed, received, or held by a facility registered under this section has a reasonable probability of causing serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals, the Secretary may by order suspend the registration of a facility—
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(1)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (A) that created, caused, or was otherwise responsible for such reasonable probability; or
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(1)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (B)(i) that knew of, or had reason to know of, such reasonable probability; and
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(1)(B)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(1)(B)(i)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (ii) packed, received, or held such food.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(1)(B)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(1)(B)(ii)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The Secretary shall provide the registrant subject to an order under paragraph (1) with an opportunity for an informal hearing, to be held as soon as possible but not later than 2 business days after the issuance of the order or such other time period, as agreed upon by the Secretary and the registrant, on the actions required for reinstatement of registration and why the registration that is subject to suspension should be reinstated. The Secretary shall reinstate a registration if the Secretary determines, based on evidence presented, that adequate grounds do not exist to continue the suspension of the registration.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(2)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (3) Post-hearing corrective action plan; vacating of order
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(3)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: If, after providing opportunity for an informal hearing under paragraph (2), the Secretary determines that the suspension of registration remains necessary, the Secretary shall require the registrant to submit a corrective action plan to demonstrate how the registrant plans to correct the conditions found by the Secretary. The Secretary shall review such plan not later than 14 days after the submission of the corrective action plan or such other time period as determined by the Secretary.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(3)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(3)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: Upon a determination by the Secretary that adequate grounds do not exist to continue the suspension actions required by the order, or that such actions should be modified, the Secretary shall promptly vacate the order and reinstate the registration of the facility subject to the order or modify the order, as appropriate.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(3)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(3)(B)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: If the registration of a facility is suspended under this subsection, no person shall import or export food into the United States from such facility, offer to import or export food into the United States from such facility, or otherwise introduce food from such facility into interstate or intrastate commerce in the United States.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(4)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The Secretary shall promulgate regulations to implement this subsection. The Secretary may promulgate such regulations on an interim final basis.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(5)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(5)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The Secretary may require that registration under this section be submitted in an electronic format. Such requirement may not take effect before the date that is 5 years after January 4, 2011.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(5)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(5)(B)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: Facilities shall be subject to the requirements of this subsection beginning on the earlier of—
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(6) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(6)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (A) the date on which the Secretary issues regulations under paragraph (5); or
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(6)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(6)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (B) 180 days after January 4, 2011.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(6)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(6)(B)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: The authority conferred by this subsection to issue an order to suspend a registration or vacate an order of suspension shall not be delegated to any officer or employee other than the Commissioner.
label: FD&C Act § 415(b)(7) [21 U.S.C. 350d(b)(7)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: For purposes of this section:
label: FD&C Act § 415(c) [21 U.S.C. 350d(c)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (1) The term "facility" includes any factory, warehouse, or establishment (including a factory, warehouse, or establishment of an importer) that manufactures, processes, packs, or holds food. Such term does not include farms; restaurants; other retail food establishments; nonprofit food establishments in which food is prepared for or served directly to the consumer; or fishing vessels (except such vessels engaged in processing as defined in section 123.3(k) of title 21, Code of Federal Regulations).
label: FD&C Act § 415(c)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350d(c)(1)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (2) The term "domestic facility" means a facility located in any of the States or Territories.
label: FD&C Act § 415(c)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350d(c)(2)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (3)(A) The term "foreign facility" means a facility that manufacturers,1 processes, packs, or holds food, but only if food from such facility is exported to the United States without further processing or packaging outside the United States.
label: FD&C Act § 415(c)(3)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350d(c)(3)(A)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: (B) A food may not be considered to have undergone further processing or packaging for purposes of subparagraph (A) solely on the basis that labeling was added or that any similar activity of a de minimis nature was carried out with respect to the food.
label: FD&C Act § 415(c)(3)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350d(c)(3)(B)]

heading: Registration of food facilities
body_text: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the Secretary to require an application, review, or licensing process for a facility to be registered, except with respect to the reinstatement of a registration that is suspended under subsection (b).
label: FD&C Act § 415(d) [21 U.S.C. 350d(d)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: In this section:
label: FD&C Act § 416(a) [21 U.S.C. 350e(a)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The term "bulk vehicle" includes a tank truck, hopper truck, rail tank car, hopper car, cargo tank, portable tank, freight container, or hopper bin, and any other vehicle in which food is shipped in bulk, with the food coming into direct contact with the vehicle.
label: FD&C Act § 416(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350e(a)(1)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The term "transportation" means any movement in commerce by motor vehicle or rail vehicle.
label: FD&C Act § 416(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350e(a)(2)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The Secretary shall by regulation require shippers, carriers by motor vehicle or rail vehicle, receivers, and other persons engaged in the transportation of food to use sanitary transportation practices prescribed by the Secretary to ensure that food is not transported under conditions that may render the food adulterated.
label: FD&C Act § 416(b) [21 U.S.C. 350e(b)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The regulations under subsection (b) shall—
label: FD&C Act § 416(c) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (1) prescribe such practices as the Secretary determines to be appropriate relating to—
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (A) sanitation;
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(A)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (B) packaging, isolation, and other protective measures;
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(B)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (C) limitations on the use of vehicles;
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(C)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (D) information to be disclosed—
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(D)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (i) to a carrier by a person arranging for the transport of food; and
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(D)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(D)(i)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (ii) to a manufacturer or other person that—
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(D)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(D)(ii)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (I) arranges for the transportation of food by a carrier; or
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(D)(ii)(I) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(D)(ii)(I)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (II) furnishes a tank vehicle or bulk vehicle for the transportation of food; and
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(D)(ii)(II) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(D)(ii)(II)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (E) recordkeeping; and
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(1)(E) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(1)(E)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (2) include—
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(2)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (A) a list of nonfood products that the Secretary determines may, if shipped in a bulk vehicle, render adulterated food that is subsequently transported in the same vehicle; and
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(2)(A)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (B) a list of nonfood products that the Secretary determines may, if shipped in a motor vehicle or rail vehicle (other than a tank vehicle or bulk vehicle), render adulterated food that is simultaneously or subsequently transported in the same vehicle.
label: FD&C Act § 416(c)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350e(c)(2)(B)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The Secretary may waive any requirement under this section, with respect to any class of persons, vehicles, food, or nonfood products, if the Secretary determines that the waiver—
label: FD&C Act § 416(d)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350e(d)(1)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (A) will not result in the transportation of food under conditions that would be unsafe for human or animal health; and
label: FD&C Act § 416(d)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350e(d)(1)(A)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (B) will not be contrary to the public interest.
label: FD&C Act § 416(d)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350e(d)(1)(B)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register any waiver and the reasons for the waiver.
label: FD&C Act § 416(d)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350e(d)(2)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: A requirement of a State or political subdivision of a State that concerns the transportation of food is preempted if—
label: FD&C Act § 416(e)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350e(e)(1)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (A) complying with a requirement of the State or political subdivision and a requirement of this section, or a regulation prescribed under this section, is not possible; or
label: FD&C Act § 416(e)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350e(e)(1)(A)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: (B) the requirement of the State or political subdivision as applied or enforced is an obstacle to accomplishing and carrying out this section or a regulation prescribed under this section.
label: FD&C Act § 416(e)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350e(e)(1)(B)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: This subsection applies to transportation that occurs on or after the effective date of the regulations promulgated under subsection (b).
label: FD&C Act § 416(e)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350e(e)(2)]

heading: Sanitary transportation practices
body_text: The Secretary of Transportation, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, and the heads of other Federal agencies, as appropriate, shall provide assistance on request, to the extent resources are available, to the Secretary for the purposes of carrying out this section.
label: FD&C Act § 416(f) [21 U.S.C. 350e(f)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: In this section:
label: FD&C Act § 417(a) [21 U.S.C. 350f(a)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The term "responsible party", with respect to an article of food, means a person that submits the registration under section 350d(a) of this title for a food facility that is required to register under section 350d(a) of this title, at which such article of food is manufactured, processed, packed, or held.
label: FD&C Act § 417(a)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(a)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The term "reportable food" means an article of food (other than infant formula) for which there is a reasonable probability that the use of, or exposure to, such article of food will cause serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals.
label: FD&C Act § 417(a)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(a)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Not later than 1 year after September 27, 2007, the Secretary shall establish within the Food and Drug Administration a Reportable Food Registry to which instances of reportable food may be submitted by the Food and Drug Administration after receipt of reports under subsection (d), via an electronic portal, from—
label: FD&C Act § 417(b)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(b)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) Federal, State, and local public health officials; or
label: FD&C Act § 417(b)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(b)(1)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) responsible parties.
label: FD&C Act § 417(b)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(b)(1)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The Secretary shall promptly review and assess the information submitted under paragraph (1) for the purposes of identifying reportable food, submitting entries to the Reportable Food Registry, acting under subsection (c), and exercising other existing food safety authorities under this chapter to protect the public health.
label: FD&C Act § 417(b)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(b)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The Secretary shall issue, or cause to be issued, an alert or a notification with respect to a reportable food using information from the Reportable Food Registry as the Secretary deems necessary to protect the public health.
top_caption: Issuance of an alert by the Secretary
label: FD&C Act § 417(c)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(c)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Paragraph (1) shall not affect the authority of the Secretary to issue an alert or a notification under any other provision of this chapter.
top_caption: Issuance of an alert by the Secretary
label: FD&C Act § 417(c)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(c)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Except as provided in paragraph (2), as soon as practicable, but in no case later than 24 hours after a responsible party determines that an article of food is a reportable food, the responsible party shall—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) submit a report to the Food and Drug Administration through the electronic portal established under subsection (b) that includes the data elements described in subsection (e) (except the elements described in paragraphs (8), (9), and (10) of such subsection); and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(1)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) investigate the cause of the adulteration if the adulteration of the article of food may have originated with the responsible party.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(1)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: A responsible party is not required to submit a report under paragraph (1) if—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) the adulteration originated with the responsible party;
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) the responsible party detected the adulteration prior to any transfer to another person of such article of food; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (C) the responsible party—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)(C)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (i) corrected such adulteration; or
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2)(C)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)(C)(i)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (ii) destroyed or caused the destruction of such article of food.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(2)(C)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(2)(C)(ii)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: A Federal, State, or local public health official may submit a report about a reportable food to the Food and Drug Administration through the electronic portal established under subsection (b) that includes the data elements described in subsection (e) that the official is able to provide.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(3)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The Secretary shall ensure that, upon submission of a report under paragraph (1) or (3), a unique number is issued through the electronic portal established under subsection (b) to the person submitting such report, by which the Secretary is able to link reports about the reportable food submitted and amended under this subsection and identify the supply chain for such reportable food.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(4)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The Secretary shall promptly review a report submitted under paragraph (1) or (3).
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(5) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(5)]

heading: Reportable food registry
paragraph_heading: Response to report submitted by a responsible party
body_text: After consultation with the responsible party that submitted a report under paragraph (1), the Secretary may require such responsible party to perform, as soon as practicable, but in no case later than a time specified by the Secretary, 1 or more of the following:
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) Amend the report submitted by the responsible party under paragraph (1) to include the data element described in subsection (e)(9).
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) Provide a notification—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (i) to the immediate previous source of the article of food, if the Secretary deems necessary;
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(i)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (ii) to the immediate subsequent recipient of the article of food, if the Secretary deems necessary; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(ii)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (iii) that includes—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(iii) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(iii)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (I) the data elements described in subsection (e) that the Secretary deems necessary;
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(iii)(I) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(iii)(I)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (II) the actions described under paragraph (7) that the recipient of the notification shall perform, as required by the Secretary; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(iii)(II) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(iii)(II)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (III) any other information that the Secretary may require.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(6)(B)(iii)(III) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(6)(B)(iii)(III)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Except as provided in paragraph (8), the Secretary may require a responsible party to perform, as soon as practicable, but in no case later than a time specified by the Secretary, after the responsible party receives a notification under subparagraph (C) or paragraph (6)(B), 1 or more of the following:
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) Submit a report to the Food and Drug Administration through the electronic portal established under subsection (b) that includes those data elements described in subsection (e) and other information that the Secretary deems necessary.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) Investigate the cause of the adulteration if the adulteration of the article of food may have originated with the responsible party.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (C) Provide a notification—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (i) to the immediate previous source of the article of food, if the Secretary deems necessary;
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(i) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(i)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (ii) to the immediate subsequent recipient of the article of food, if the Secretary deems necessary; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(ii) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(ii)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (iii) that includes—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(iii) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(iii)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (I) the data elements described in subsection (e) that the Secretary deems necessary;
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(iii)(I) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(iii)(I)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (II) the actions described under this paragraph that the recipient of the notification shall perform, as required by the Secretary; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(iii)(II) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(iii)(II)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (III) any other information that the Secretary may require.
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(7)(C)(iii)(III) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(7)(C)(iii)(III)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: If a responsible party receives a notification under paragraph (6)(B) or paragraph (7)(C) with respect to an article of food after the responsible party has submitted a report to the Food and Drug Administration under paragraph (1) with respect to such article of food—
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(8) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(8)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) the responsible party is not required to submit an additional report or make a notification under paragraph (7); and
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(8)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(8)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) the responsible party shall amend the report submitted by the responsible party under paragraph (1) to include the data elements described in paragraph (9), and, with respect to both such notification and such report, paragraph (11) of subsection (e).
label: FD&C Act § 417(d)(8)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(d)(8)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The data elements described in this subsection are the following:
label: FD&C Act § 417(e) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (1) The registration numbers of the responsible party under section 350d(a)(3) 1 of this title.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (2) The date on which an article of food was determined to be a reportable food.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (3) A description of the article of food including the quantity or amount.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(3)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (4) The extent and nature of the adulteration.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(4)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (5) If the adulteration of the article of food may have originated with the responsible party, the results of the investigation required under paragraph (1)(B) or (7)(B) of subsection (d), as applicable and when known.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(5) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(5)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (6) The disposition of the article of food, when known.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(6) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(6)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (7) Product information typically found on packaging including product codes, use-by dates, and names of manufacturers, packers, or distributors sufficient to identify the article of food.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(7) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(7)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (8) Contact information for the responsible party.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(8) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(8)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (9) The contact information for parties directly linked in the supply chain and notified under paragraph (6)(B) or (7)(C) of subsection (d), as applicable.
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(9) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(9)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (10) The information required by the Secretary to be included in a notification provided by the responsible party involved under paragraph (6)(B) or (7)(C) of subsection (d) or required in a report under subsection (d)(7)(A).
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(10) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(10)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (11) The unique number described in subsection (d)(4).
label: FD&C Act § 417(e)(11) [21 U.S.C. 350f(e)(11)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Except with respect to fruits and vegetables that are raw agricultural commodities, not more than 18 months after January 4, 2011, the Secretary may require a responsible party to submit to the Secretary consumer-oriented information regarding a reportable food, which shall include—
label: FD&C Act § 417(f) [21 U.S.C. 350f(f)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (1) a description of the article of food as provided in subsection (e)(3);
label: FD&C Act § 417(f)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(f)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (2) as provided in subsection (e)(7), affected product identification codes, such as UPC, SKU, or lot or batch numbers sufficient for the consumer to identify the article of food;
label: FD&C Act § 417(f)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(f)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (3) contact information for the responsible party as provided in subsection (e)(8); and
label: FD&C Act § 417(f)(3) [21 U.S.C. 350f(f)(3)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (4) any other information the Secretary determines is necessary to enable a consumer to accurately identify whether such consumer is in possession of the reportable food.
label: FD&C Act § 417(f)(4) [21 U.S.C. 350f(f)(4)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The Secretary shall—
label: FD&C Act § 417(g)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(g)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) prepare the critical information described under subsection (f) for a reportable food as a standardized one-page summary;
label: FD&C Act § 417(g)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(g)(1)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) publish such one-page summary on the Internet website of the Food and Drug Administration in a format that can be easily printed by a grocery store for purposes of consumer notification.
label: FD&C Act § 417(g)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(g)(1)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: A notification described under paragraph (1)(B) shall include the date and time such summary was posted on the Internet website of the Food and Drug Administration.
label: FD&C Act § 417(g)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(g)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: If a grocery store sold a reportable food that is the subject of the posting and such establishment is part of 2 chain of establishments with 15 or more physical locations, then such establishment shall, not later than 24 hours after a one page summary described in subsection (g) is published, prominently display such summary or the information from such summary via at least one of the methods identified under paragraph (2) and maintain the display for 14 days.
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Not more than 1 year after January 4, 2011, the Secretary shall develop and publish a list of acceptable conspicuous locations and manners, from which grocery stores shall select at least one, for providing the notification required in paragraph (1). Such list shall include—
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) posting the notification at or near the register;
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(2)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) providing the location of the reportable food;
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(2)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (C) providing targeted recall information given to customers upon purchase of a food; and
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(2)(C) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(2)(C)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (D) other such prominent and conspicuous locations and manners utilized by grocery stores as of January 4, 2011, to provide notice of such recalls to consumers as considered appropriate by the Secretary.
label: FD&C Act § 417(h)(2)(D) [21 U.S.C. 350f(h)(2)(D)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: In implementing this section, the Secretary shall—
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(1)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) share information and coordinate regulatory efforts with the Department of Agriculture; and
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(1)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) if the Secretary receives a report submitted about a food within the jurisdiction of the Department of Agriculture, promptly provide such report to the Department of Agriculture.
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(1)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: In implementing this section, the Secretary shall work with the State and local public health officials to share information and coordinate regulatory efforts, in order to—
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(2) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(2)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (A) help to ensure coverage of the safety of the food supply chain, including those food establishments regulated by the States and localities that are not required to register under section 350d of this title; and
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(2)(A)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: (B) reduce duplicative regulatory efforts.
top_caption: Coordination of Federal, State, and local efforts
label: FD&C Act § 417(i)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350f(i)(2)(B)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: The responsible party shall maintain records related to each report received, notification made, and report submitted to the Food and Drug Administration under this section for 2 years. A responsible party shall, at the request of the Secretary, permit inspection of such records as provided for section 3 350c of this title.
label: FD&C Act § 417(j) [21 U.S.C. 350f(j)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: Except as provided by section 350d(a)(4) 1 of this title, section 552 of title 5 shall apply to any request for information regarding a record in the Reportable Food Registry.
label: FD&C Act § 417(k) [21 U.S.C. 350f(k)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: A report or notification under subsection (d) shall be considered to be a safety report under section 379v of this title and may be accompanied by a statement, which shall be part of any report released for public disclosure, that denies that the report or the notification constitutes an admission that the product involved caused or contributed to a death, serious injury, or serious illness.
label: FD&C Act § 417(l) [21 U.S.C. 350f(l)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: A report or notification under this section shall not be considered an admission that the article of food involved is adulterated or caused or contributed to a death, serious injury, or serious illness.
label: FD&C Act § 417(m) [21 U.S.C. 350f(m)]

heading: Reportable food registry
body_text: If, after receiving a report under subsection (d), the Secretary believes such food may have been deliberately adulterated, the Secretary shall immediately notify the Secretary of Homeland Security. The Secretary shall make relevant information from the Reportable Food Registry available to the Secretary of Homeland Security.
label: FD&C Act § 417(n) [21 U.S.C. 350f(n)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: The owner, operator, or agent in charge of a facility shall, in accordance with this section, evaluate the hazards that could affect food manufactured, processed, packed, or held by such facility, identify and implement preventive controls to significantly minimize or prevent the occurrence of such hazards and provide assurances that such food is not adulterated under section 342 of this title or misbranded under section 343(w) of this title, monitor the performance of those controls, and maintain records of this monitoring as a matter of routine practice.
label: FD&C Act § 418(a) [21 U.S.C. 350g(a)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: The owner, operator, or agent in charge of a facility shall—
label: FD&C Act § 418(b) [21 U.S.C. 350g(b)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: (1) identify and evaluate known or reasonably foreseeable hazards that may be associated with the facility, including—
label: FD&C Act § 418(b)(1) [21 U.S.C. 350g(b)(1)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: (A) biological, chemical, physical, and radiological hazards, natural toxins, pesticides, drug residues, decomposition, parasites, allergens, and unapproved food and color additives; and
label: FD&C Act § 418(b)(1)(A) [21 U.S.C. 350g(b)(1)(A)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: (B) hazards that occur naturally, or may be unintentionally introduced; and
label: FD&C Act § 418(b)(1)(B) [21 U.S.C. 350g(b)(1)(B)]

heading: Hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls
body_text: (2) identify and evaluate hazards that may be intentionally introduced, including by acts of terrorism; and
